solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good, pink paper for wrapping one's present

indicators.note: the paper and the good together are there for wrapping, so they go round the one

parts.note: the Financial Times, printed on pink paper, is the FT
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a birthday present in pink paper, which looks like a good choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a British newspaper printed on pink paper. G and FT wrap around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a present, the thing given; they are plain synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Pop producers putting sum of money on promotions

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
ads, advertisements, promote products

explanation.surface: A record company spends a large sum promoting its pop acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop producers' looks like the music business, but a pop is a father, and a grandad produced him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a word for father, so grandfathers are the ones who produced each pop.

clue.text: Lots to eat? Suffolk runs out!

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the county of Suffolk has run out of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is an English county. 'out' tells you to rearrange SUFFOLK with R added.
explanation.definitionFit: A forkful is the quantity a fork carries, so several of them are amounts of food lifted to the mouth.

clue.text: Certain Americans developing British mania, alas

indicators.note: developing means the letters take a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some Americans regret, alas, that they are catching a craze for all things British.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the US state of Alabama are a particular group of Americans.

clue.text: High capital growth ultimately when investing in the City

indicators.note: investing in means going inside, so these letters are put within the city

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the city

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of growth

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'

explanation.surface: A financial note about capital growth when someone invests in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the City' suggests the London financial district, but here it is LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa, the Tibetan capital, sits at about 3,650 metres, one of the world's loftiest capital cities.

clue.text: Piece of music which Swiss hero managed not to broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to send out on air, so the answer is what the phrase sounds like spoken

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss hero, dodged capture, so he managed not to be bagged: what he avoided was to 'bag a Tell'

explanation.surface: Asks for a piece of music the Swiss hero William Tell somehow avoided putting on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'bag a Tell', the catch William Tell escaped, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a short, light composition for piano, such as Beethoven's Für Elise.

clue.text: With command from military, Gaels dispersed

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gaelic soldiers scatter when ordered to by a military commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting magisterially means behaving with authority, in the manner of a master or magistrate.

clue.text: Out of a book, one fed yarn

parts.note: a loom is a machine you feed yarn into for weaving

explanation.surface: Someone strings a tall tale out of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word: 'Out' as in flowers being out.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out have opened, so a plant in bloom is out.

clue.text: Strut made of wood for example holds

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the first word goes round the wood

parts.note: say means for example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'
ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A structural strut made from timber, something like holly or oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strut' looks like a beam of wood but it is a verb for walking.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a showy, swaggering way, which is to strut.

clue.text: Roman general, an old man, assuming control

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the article and old man take control inside them

parts.note: an gives A, the indefinite article
pa is a word for father, one's old man
to have a grip on something is to control it

explanation.surface: An elderly Roman general takes command.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman commander who won the battle of Actium for Augustus.

clue.text: Near miss, perhaps: too close for comfort?

definitions.note: near is an old sense meaning mean or stingy

parts.note: Penny is one example of a girl's name, a miss
something pinching, like a tight shoe, fits too close for comfort

explanation.surface: A near miss that was too close for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near miss' reads as one phrase; split it: 'Near' is the definition, meaning miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: Near in its old British sense means tight-fisted, and penny-pinching is miserly.

clue.text: Typical farmer astride gee-gee is a funny fit!

indicators.note: astride means with legs either side, so the farmer sits around the horse

parts.note: Farmer Giles is the stock name for a typical English farmer
GG is short for gee-gee, a horse

explanation.surface: A farmer riding a horse is a comic sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is the British stock name for a typical rural farmer; gee-gee is a childish word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The giggles are a fit of uncontrollable laughter, which is what something funny brings on.

clue.text: Excellent ambition by worker perhaps to get one up

parts.note: def is slang for excellent
an end is an aim or ambition
a worker ant is one example of a worker

explanation.surface: A worker gets ahead with great ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one up' looks like getting ahead, but it is someone up before a court.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is up in court faces the charge, which makes them the accused party.

clue.text: Tongue? Hold it, with oxtail initially not available

parts.note: sh is a call to hold it and be quiet

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of oxtail

explanation.surface: At a restaurant, someone is told to hold their tongue because oxtail is off the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like the meat but is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Shona is a Bantu language spoken in Zimbabwe, and tongue is an old word for a language.

clue.text: Herb repelled Scottish devil woman — but took his time?

parts.note: dill is a herb

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the devil and the woman are read backwards

parts.note: deil is the Scots word for the devil
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A man takes his time over a herb that drove off a Scottish devil woman.
explanation.walkthrough: DEIL is Scots for devil; reading DEIL LADY backwards gives YDALLIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilly-dally is to dawdle or waste time, so the past tense means lingered.

clue.text: Light seen by a lord quietly embracing religion

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the religion goes inside

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
Islam is a religion

explanation.surface: A lord is seen quietly taking up a religion, as if enlightened.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aldis lamp is a signalling lamp used by navies to flash Morse code.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aldis lamp is a handheld signal lamp, a type of light for sending messages.

clue.text: Tir nan-Og strangely left out of the picture?

indicators.note: strangely means oddly arranged, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The Irish land of eternal youth has strangely been left out of a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Tír na nÓg is the otherworld of Irish myth, the land of the young.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left out of the picture is uninformed, lacking knowledge of what is happening.

clue.text: Small fish sandwiches I polish off with large cordial

indicators.note: sandwiches means encloses between two parts, so the fish goes around

parts.note: fry are young, small fish
to polish off something is to end it

explanation.surface: A diner finishes off whitebait sandwiches with a big glass of cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like a fruit drink but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial as an adjective means warm and amiable, which is what a friendly manner is.

clue.text: Long digital film dealt unusually with gender ID

definitions.note: digital is used as a noun here, meaning a digit

indicators.note: cards dealt unusually come out in a strange order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lengthy streamed film has an odd approach to gender identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long digital film' reads as a streaming movie; the definition stops at 'digital', used as a noun for a digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the five fingers, the middle one is the longest digit on the hand.

clue.text: Not exactly a family affair following

parts.note: kin are one's family
a do is a party or affair
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Describes a family party that is not quite what it claims to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is kind of so means it is only approximately or somewhat so.

clue.text: Girl with touching article

parts.note: and joins things together, as with does
re means concerning or touching on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl with a touching article in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Disown niece, oddly out of order

definitions.note: an adjective describing one of the classical orders of architecture

indicators.note: oddly out means the odd-numbered letters are taken away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone disowns a niece who behaved badly, out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' looks like a single phrase meaning badly behaved, but 'out' belongs with 'oddly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, with scroll-shaped capitals on its columns.

clue.text: Sort of weapon taken from NCO was carried by everyone

parts.note: an SM, sergeant major, is a non-commissioned officer
all means everyone
bore is the past tense of bear, so something bore means it was carried

explanation.surface: A weapon is taken from an NCO and passed round everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-bore rifle has a narrow barrel, so the term names a class of firearm.

clue.text: Firing from big guns upset native

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's big guns
a native son is someone born in a place

explanation.surface: A local is upset by the firing of heavy artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing' looks like guns going off, but here it means setting fire to things.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, a sense of firing.

clue.text: Philosopher's nadir: redundant, in retreat, diminished

definitions.note: the possessive 's is a link meaning 'is'

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so those letters are read in reverse
diminished means cut down, so only part of these words is kept, the letters within them

explanation.surface: A philosopher's low point: losing his job, withdrawing, and feeling smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards across nADIR REDundant.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Derrida was the French thinker who founded deconstruction.

clue.text: Kenny's outside cutting turf up

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the letters go inside the turf

parts.note: sward is an expanse of grassy turf

indicators.note: outside points to the outer letters of Kenny's name

explanation.surface: Kenny is outdoors, cutting up the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside letters of Kenny are K and Y; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyward means towards the sky, the direction above.

clue.text: Filling one glass after female called

indicators.note: after sends the one and the glass second, behind the female who called

parts.note: rang means phoned or called
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pane is a sheet of glass

explanation.surface: A woman rings up after filling a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the female and called ahead of the one and glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipane is an almond cream used to fill tarts and pastries.

clue.text: Postponement indeed on the way

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so indeed comes second behind the way

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
ay is an old word for yes or indeed

explanation.surface: A delay indeed occurs while on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution is a legal suspension, the deferral of a sentence.
